# SRP proof fixture

`TestCalculateProofMatchesFastlaneSIRP` uses proofs generated by
[fastlane-sirp at revision 93d14c4e921b0b0408198756b32e1757f8f7e6a8](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane-sirp/tree/93d14c4e921b0b0408198756b32e1757f8f7e6a8).
The upstream [client](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane-sirp/blob/93d14c4e921b0b0408198756b32e1757f8f7e6a8/lib/fastlane-sirp/client.rb)
and [proof calculations](https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane-sirp/blob/93d14c4e921b0b0408198756b32e1757f8f7e6a8/lib/fastlane-sirp/sirp.rb)
are independent of the Go implementation.

Inputs: 2048-bit group, client secret `a = 123456`, server public value
`B = 2`, username `dev@example.com`, password `secret`, salt `salt`,
protocol `s2k`, one PBKDF2 iteration, and a 32-byte derived password.
The fixed client secret is injected only to make this test fixture repeatable.

Run the following with Ruby and its OpenSSL standard library. Verified with
Ruby 3.2.0. It downloads the pinned source into a temporary directory; no gems
or project dependencies are installed.

```sh
fixture_dir=$(mktemp -d)
git clone --quiet https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane-sirp.git "$fixture_dir"
git -C "$fixture_dir" checkout --quiet 93d14c4e921b0b0408198756b32e1757f8f7e6a8
ruby -I "$fixture_dir/lib" <<'RUBY'
require 'fastlane-sirp'
require 'base64'

client = SIRP::Client.new(2048)
client.instance_variable_set(:@a, 123456)
client.start_authentication
password = OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(
  Digest::SHA256.digest('secret'), 'salt', 1, 32, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new
)
m1 = client.process_challenge(
  'dev@example.com', password.unpack1('H*'), 'salt'.unpack1('H*'), '02',
  is_password_encrypted: true
)
puts Base64.strict_encode64([m1].pack('H*'))
puts Base64.strict_encode64([client.H_AMK].pack('H*'))
RUBY
rm -rf "$fixture_dir"
```

Expected output, in `m1`, `m2` order:

```text
OL3tMhvYaZcmgV8KO40CG1UZ6Rgw4dDF1bSGsEN6c4s=
548X9ZQ5iGyqHhSBA3s2lDdzcZThics3GqSP20346T0=
```
